title: Column grouping, resizing gestures, and density presets for virtualized table
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our existing table component lacks affordances for grouped columns, consistent resize gestures across density modes, and clear defaults for density presets. Virtualized tables introduce complexity for resizing and filtering because column widths and DOM recycling create measurement and focus challenges. Goals: (1) Design a column grouping model with visual grouping headers and collapsible groups, (2) define consistent drag/keyboard resize interactions that work reliably in virtualized contexts and across density modes, (3) introduce three density presets (Comfortable / Compact / Tight) with token mappings and spacing guidelines, (4) improve sorting/filtering discoverability with a sticky filter row and multi-column sort affordance, and (5) document accessibility requirements and performance implications for engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Designs for column groups including collapsed/expanded state, group header affordances, and chevron animation are in Figma and linked.
Resize interaction spec: drag handle hit target, double-click auto-fit, and keyboard (Ctrl+Arrow / Enter to edit width) documented.
Three density presets defined with token values (row height, vertical padding, icon sizes) and example screenshots for each mode.
Virtualization guidance: visual placeholders and sticky header shadow behavior specified; resizing should not break virtualization or cause excessive reflows.
Accessibility checklist completed (ARIA roles for column groups, keyboard resizing, screen reader announcements), reviewed by accessibility specialist.
Engineering tickets created for runtime changes (ENG-5922, ENG-6130) and a PR exists for UI styles (github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-ui/pull/489).
design_notes: Key principle: keep DOM stable and minimize measurement on scroll. For grouped columns we introduce a separate group header row above column headers; collapsing a group hides its child columns via width:0 + aria-hidden instead of removing DOM nodes to avoid virtualization churn. Resize handles are positioned at column edges and use a 16px invisible hit target that appears on hover/focus. Density presets map to tokens: comfortable -> token.rowHeight.3, compact -> token.rowHeight.2, tight -> token.rowHeight.1; these feed into cell padding, icon spacing, and keyboard target sizes. Sorting UI: clicking a column header toggles sort (asc/desc/none), shift-click adds to multi-sort; persistent multi-sort chips show in the sticky filter row with drag-to-reorder for priority.
decisions: Use a non-destructive collapse for column groups (width transitions) to avoid virtualization DOM churn.
Expose an API prop 'density' with values 'comfortable'|'compact'|'tight' and fall back to system spacing tokens.
Keep the visible resize hit target larger than visual handle (micro-affordance) to improve touch/trackpad usability.
Implement sticky filter row rather than inline per-header filters to reduce layout thrashing in virtualized lists.
tradeoffs: Non-destructive collapse increases CSS complexity (width:0 plus transitions) but avoids expensive remounts while virtualizing.
Larger hit targets slightly reduce horizontal space for narrow columns; for very narrow columns we cap minimum width and show tooltip for overflow.
Multi-column sorting in UI increases visual complexity; chosen to improve power-user workflows at the cost of slightly denser header UI.
